source_judgments: PROTECTED specification is module-only; descendant access and PRIVATE accessibility are different conditions. USE renaming/re-export preserves the entity's attribute.
C859's nonpointer definition contexts and C860's pointer association contexts remain separate. Calling an owner procedure does not waive an outside caller's prohibited defining actual.

Pointer components are subobjects in association contexts, not their pointees. An ordinary alias sharing a target is distinct from a pointer dummy argument-associated with the protected pointer actual.

Target-loss, BLOCK, RETURN and END exceptions retain their actual premises. Reset through the owner precedes later association inquiry; SAVE does not extend a dead target or an internal procedure's host lifetime.

SAVE retains actual association/allocation/definition/value through the specified events; it does not imply initial definedness. Recursive sharing and sequential persistence require different finite witnesses.
Implicit main/module/submodule SAVE, explicit initialization, DATA, default initialization and BIND routes keep their distinct canonical owners.

Common-block SAVE confers attributes through the block while C862 forbids specification on a member. The cross-scope obligation has a nonexempt antecedent; blank-common retention does not establish a SAVE declaration.
All90facets remain pending. Existing BIND-common effect/control, initialization, finalization, entry-capture and S10 cases retain owners, roles and reviews.
